A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same newspaper-AI audit. All 27 pages in each version, including Appendices A–C, are readable and support comparison of text, figures and tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original analyses of three newspaper corpora, longitudinal reporter data, detector agreement and a manual disclosure audit of 100 articles.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical analyses and reports revised ownership-related results in Section 3.1 and Figure 3.

M1.justification: The Pangram detection pipeline, three-category label mapping, Qwen3-8B topic classification and newspaper metadata matching remain unchanged in Section 2 and Appendices A–B.

E1.justification: Both versions use recent_news, opinions and ai_reporters with unchanged reported temporal, geographic and language coverage. Removing an illustrative op-ed from Table 4 does not establish its removal from the underlying corpus.

E2.justification: GPTZero remains the evaluated comparator to Pangram in Section 2.4 and Appendix B. No comparison method is added, removed or replaced.

E3.justification: The reported collection procedures, validation settings, balanced 1,000-article detector comparison and appendix analysis protocols are unchanged. Neither PDF documents a protocol revision explaining the changed ownership rates.

E4.justification: The illustrative op-ed cases are narrowed by removing Joshua Claybourn's article from Table 4. Section 4 substitutes Nicole Saphier as an example, although she already appeared in v1's table. Other case studies and appendix robustness analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Agreement statistics, significance tests, descriptive variability and effect-size reporting are unchanged, including the Welch and Mann–Whitney analyses in Appendix C.1. No repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Section 3.1 and Figure 3 revise Boone's overall AI-use rate from 20.9% to 18.3%, technology from 58.3% to 66.7%, and lifestyle from 32.9% to 47.1%, alongside other Boone topic-cell revisions. Boone remains highest overall. Table 4 removes the Claybourn detection example; aggregate findings and appendix results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs. Operational definitions, label mappings and mathematical criteria such as duplicate-similarity thresholds remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: widespread but uneven AI use, roughly 9% prevalence in recent news, a 6.4-fold opinion/news contrast and rare disclosure.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning ownership, guest contributors and disclosure remain unchanged. Both retain the same qualifications about detector fallibility, mixed authorship, sampling, language coverage and data accessibility.

D1.justification: The collection and preprocessing tools, topic-classification prompt, detector API and label-mapping details, and general dataset/code/dashboard access statements are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited research and positioning as a first large-scale newspaper-AI audit are unchanged.

P1.justification: Language editing is limited to the guest-contributor example and version/date header. The section sequence, explanatory prose and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3 reorders topic columns and updates the Boone row's displayed values and colors. Table 4 loses one row and reflows. Other figures, tables and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 revises Boone's rates and removes the Claybourn example without explaining their basis or providing new validation. Both versions otherwise retain the same methods, central evidence and limitations. The PDFs therefore do not establish whether these localized revisions improve accuracy or simply alter the reported evidence.
